newsitem.title: ITALY: TIM had 5.7 million subscribers end-1996. [CORRECTED 10:54 GMT]
newsitem.headline: TIM had 5.7 million subscribers end-1996. [CORRECTED 10:54 GMT]

text.p: Italy's state-controlled mobile phone company Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) said that it had 5.7 million mobile phone subscribers by the end of 1996.

In a statement, the group said that at the year-end TIM had 5,700,312 subscribers including 1,910,000 GSM digital users, compared with 3,863,374 a year earlier, for a gain of 47 percent (corrects from 33 percent).

TIM said that over 1.9 million new customers chose to buy a TIM mobile phone in 1996, surpassing the group's success in 1995 when TIM posted one of the highest growth rates in the world with 1.623 million new subscribers.

TIM's only competitor in the Italian mobile phone market, the consortium Omnitel which is 35.5 percent controlled by Olivetti, said on Wednesday that it had gained 713,000 GSM phone subscribers in the 13 months since it launched its service in December 1995.

TIM said that its TIM card, a rechargeable prepaid GSM card, provided a substantial contribution to TIM's success. About 80,000 cards were sold during the three days before Christmas, bringing the total number of new customers to 570,000 just three months after the product's launch.
The card has been successful beyond all expectations and has created a new pay-as-you-go market segment in Italy which is expected to number six million by the year 2000, TIM said.
It added that since there are no fixed monthly charges and the cost of telephone calls cannot exceed the prepaid amount it gives consumers absolute control over their budgets.
TIM's total number of mobile phone subscribers include GSM digital and also analogue users, while Omnitel has only GSM users.
